# SMCraft / Stateloom — State Machine Craft (Full Reference)

> Design, validate, generate and run hierarchical state machines. One declarative format (SMDF) is read by an engine, a code generator, an MCP server, a terminal CLI, a socket.io hub and a browser canvas — so an agent, a person at a shell and a person at a canvas can edit the same document while it is open, and each sees the others' edits arrive.

**Engine (npm):** `@miadi/stateloom-engine` 0.4.3 — renamed from `smcraft`, which is deprecated on npm — parser, validator, runtime, SMDF interpreter, Python + TypeScript codegen
**Engine (PyPI):** `smcraft` 0.1.5 — the Python twin, CLI `smcg`
**Protocol:** `@miadi/stateloom-protocol` 0.1.3
**Client:** `@miadi/stateloom-client` 0.1.1
**Hub:** `@miadi/stateloom` 0.1.1 — bin `smcraft-bridge`
**React:** `@miadi/stateloom-react` 0.1.4
**CLI:** `@miadi/stateloom-cli` 0.1.2 — bin `smcx`
**MCP:** `@miadi/stateloom-mcp` 0.1.3 — bins `stateloom-mcp`, `smcraft-mcp`
**Skills:** `@miadi/stateloom-skills` 0.1.0 — bin `stateloom`
**Designer:** `web/` — `"private": true`, run from the repo, never published
**Framework:** RISE v1.2 (Reverse-engineer → Intent-extract → Specify → Export)
**RISE Specs:** 70–79
**Repository:** https://github.com/jgwill/smcraft
**Published at:** https://docs.smcraft.jgwill.com

---

## 1. Architecture Overview

Two pipelines share one format. The first turns a definition into code you ship. The second keeps a definition in agreement across every surface currently looking at it.

### Generation pipeline

```
.smdf.json definition (or .smdf.xml / .fsm)
    ↓
  Parser (Spec 70)
    ↓
  EnrichedModel (lookup maps: state_map, event_map, timer_map, feeders_map, parent_map)
    ↓
  Validator (V001–V014)
    ↓
  Code Generator (Spec 72)
    ↓
  Python / TypeScript state machine classes
    ↓
  Runtime Engine (Spec 71) executes them
```

### Live pipeline

```
   agent (MCP)        terminal (smcx)        canvas (web/)
        │                    │                     │
        └────── PatchOp ─────┴──── PatchOp ────────┘
                             │
                    @miadi/stateloom (hub)
                    in-memory doc + seq per room
                    presence · chokidar external-edit differ
                             │
                    room key = ABSOLUTE project-file path
                             │
                        .smdf.json on disk
```

Mutations are durable-first everywhere: write the file, then emit the patch. A surface that cannot reach the hub still produces a correct document.

### Package Topology

```
smcraft/
├── py/                    # PyPI: smcraft 0.1.5
│   └── smcraft/           # model.py, parser.py, runtime.py, codegen.py, cli.py (smcg)
├── ts/                    # npm: @miadi/stateloom-engine 0.4.3  (was smcraft)
│   └── src/               # model.ts, parser.ts, runtime.ts, codegen.ts, index.ts,
│                          # machine.ts — the SMDF interpreter (no codegen)
├── bridge-protocol/       # npm: @miadi/stateloom-protocol 0.1.3
│   └── src/               # definition, ops (PatchOp), apply, diff, seq, events (EV),
│                          # tree, autoLayout, edgeRoutes, edgeLabels, glyphs,
│                          # exportName, env (envAlias), render/{mermaid,ascii}
├── bridge-client/         # npm: @miadi/stateloom-client 0.1.1
│   └── src/client.ts      # createBridgeClient — join/patch/full/presence
├── bridge/                # npm: @miadi/stateloom 0.1.1 — bin smcraft-bridge
│   └── src/               # hub.ts (startBridge), docio.ts, watcher.ts, bin.js
├── bridge-react/          # npm: @miadi/stateloom-react 0.1.4
│   └── src/               # session.ts, useSmcraftBridge.ts, autoLayout.ts, viewport.ts
├── cli/                   # npm: @miadi/stateloom-cli 0.1.2 — bin smcx
│   └── src/               # index.ts, docio.ts, mutate.ts, commands/, render/
├── mcp/                   # npm: @miadi/stateloom-mcp 0.1.3
│   └── src/               # server.ts (15 tools, 1 resource, 1 prompt), projectSwitch.ts
├── skills-cli/            # npm: @miadi/stateloom-skills 0.1.0 — bin stateloom
├── skills/                # the six skill sources the CLI installs
├── web/                   # PRIVATE — the designer app (Next.js)
├── scripts/live-loop.sh   # one absolute source of truth for the live loop
├── examples/              # Example SMDF definitions
├── rispecs/               # RISE specifications 70–79
└── KINSHIP.md             # Lineage and relationships
```

### Design surfaces

`smcg` (parse, validate, generate from the command line) · the Python / TypeScript API (programmatic parsing, validation, interpretation, generation) · the MCP server (agents designing conversationally) · `smcx` (drive the live loom from a terminal, render without a browser) · the web designer (drag-and-drop SVG canvas, live-synced with the others).

All five read and write the same `.smdf.json`.

---

## 2. SMDF Schema Specification

### File Format
Extension: `.smdf.json` (primary), `.smdf.xml`, `.fsm` (legacy XML)

### Top-Level Structure
```json
{
  "settings": {
    "namespace": "Trading.Strategies",
    "name": "FDBBreakoutStrategy",
    "asynchronous": false,
    "objects": [
      { "instance": "strategy", "class": "FDBBreakoutStrategyEntity" },
      { "instance": "market", "class": "MarketDataProvider" }
    ],
    "context": { "class": "FDBBreakoutContext" }
  },
  "events": [
    {
      "name": "StrategyEvents",
      "feeder": "StrategyFeeder",
      "events": [
        { "id": "Activate", "parameters": [{ "name": "strategyId", "type": "string" }] },
        { "id": "BreakoutDetected", "parameters": [{ "name": "price", "type": "float" }] },
        { "id": "FDBSignalFound" },
        { "id": "OrderFilled" }
      ],
      "timers": [{ "id": "evMaxPuiTimeout", "name": "MaxPuiTimer" }]
    }
  ],
  "state": {
    "name": "Root",
    "states": [
      {
        "name": "Created",
        "transitions": [{ "event": "Activate", "nextState": "Active_WaitingBreakout" }]
      },
      {
        "name": "Active",
        "states": [
          {
            "name": "Active_WaitingBreakout",
            "onEntry": { "actions": [{ "code": "market.start_price_monitoring(strategy.breakout_price)" }] },
            "transitions": [{ "event": "BreakoutDetected", "nextState": "Active_WaitingSignal" }]
          },
          {
            "name": "Active_WaitingSignal",
            "transitions": [{ "event": "FDBSignalFound", "nextState": "Active_WaitingEntering" }]
          },
          {
            "name": "Active_WaitingEntering",
            "transitions": [{ "event": "OrderFilled", "nextState": "Completed" }]
          }
        ]
      },
      { "name": "Completed", "kind": "final" },
      { "name": "Faulted", "kind": "final" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Settings Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `namespace` | string | ✓ | Code namespace for generated output |
| `name` | string | | State machine name (defaults to filename) |
| `asynchronous` | boolean | | If true, generates ContextAsync with event queue |
| `objects` | ObjectRef[] | | Domain objects accessible in actions/conditions |
| `context` | ContextConfig | | Override context class/instance naming |
| `using` | string[] | | Additional imports for generated code |
| `_source` | object | | Provenance. `pdeId` / `pdeFolder` let `generate_rispec` fold the originating PDE's intent, directions and ambiguities into the spec it writes. |

### ObjectRef, EventSourceDef, EventDef, TimerDef
```json
{ "instance": "strategy", "class": "BDBOStrategyEntity", "namespace": "Trading" }
```
Objects are stored on the generated Context class and reachable from action code as `context.strategy.method()`.

An **EventSourceDef** groups related events and generates a Feeder class with a typed method per event: `name` (identifier), `feeder` (generated class name), `events[]`, `timers[]`.

```json
{ "id": "OrderFilled", "parameters": [{ "name": "tradeId", "type": "string" }, { "name": "fillPrice", "type": "float" }] }
{ "id": "evTimeout", "name": "Timeout" }
```
Parameter types: `string`, `int`, `float`, `double`, `bool`, `boolean`, `object`, or custom type names. Timers generate as events; in actions they appear as `timerStart: { "timer": "Timeout", "duration": "60000" }` and `timerStop: "Timeout"`.

### StateDef

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Unique state identifier |
| `kind` | "normal" \| "final" \| "history" | State classification (default: normal) |
| `description` | string | Human-readable description |
| `onEntry` | { actions: ActionDef[] } | Entry actions |
| `onExit` | { actions: ActionDef[] } | Exit actions |
| `transitions` | TransitionDef[] | Event-triggered transitions |
| `states` | StateDef[] | Child states (makes this composite) |
| `parallel` | ParallelDef | Orthogonal regions |

**State classification (derived from structure, not declared):** leaf (`states == [] && parallel == null`), composite (`states.length > 0`), final (`kind == "final"` — no outgoing transitions, no children), history (`kind == "history"` — remembers the last active child), parallel (`parallel != null` — orthogonal regions), root (top of the tree).

### TransitionDef
```json
{
  "event": "OrderFilled",
  "nextState": "Completed",
  "condition": "strategy.validate_mpr(entry_price, stop_price)",
  "actions": [{ "code": "strategy.record_fill(trade_id, fill_price)" }]
}
```
- `event`: Required — references a defined EventDef.id
- `nextState`: Optional — if omitted, this is an internal transition (no state change)
- `condition`: Optional — guard expression; transition only fires if true
- Multiple transitions on the same event create conditional branches (if/elif/else)

### ActionDef and ParallelDef
An action takes one of three forms; a parallel block takes regions and an exit state:
```json
{ "code": "strategy.start_monitoring()" }
{ "timerStart": { "timer": "Timeout", "duration": "60000" } }
{ "timerStop": "Timeout" }

{ "nextState": "Completed",
  "states": [{ "name": "RegionA", "states": [] }, { "name": "RegionB", "states": [] }] }
```
A parallel block requires ≥2 regions, each with ≥1 child state. `nextState` is the exit state taken when all regions complete.

### Validation Rules (V001–V014)

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| V001 | Exactly one root state must be defined |
| V002 | All state names must be unique |
| V003 | All event IDs must be unique |
| V004 | Timer IDs must not collide with event IDs |
| V005 | Transition events must reference defined events |
| V006 | Transition nextState must reference defined states |
| V007 | Final states must have no outgoing transitions |
| V008 | Final states must have no children |
| V009 | Composite states must have at least one non-final initial child |
| V010 | Parallel states must have ≥2 regions, each with ≥1 child |
| V011 | Parallel region transitions must target within region or parent exit state |
| V012 | Composite states must have at least one child |
| V013 | At least one event source must be defined |
| V014 | Timer references in actions must reference defined timers |

V002 is load-bearing beyond validation: because state names are unique, `name` is the stable key the bridge's PatchOp vocabulary uses to address a state.

---

## 3. Python Package Deep Dive (`smcraft` 0.1.5, PyPI)

### Installation
```bash
pip install smcraft
# or from source:
cd py && pip install -e .
```

### Module: `smcraft.model` (Spec 70)
Dataclass-based SMDF representation.

```python
from smcraft import (
    StateMachineDefinition,  # Root: settings + event_sources + root_state
    SettingsModel, EventSourceDef, EventDef, TimerDef, ParameterDef,
    StateDef, TransitionDef, ActionDef, ParallelDef,
    ObjectRef, ContextConfig,
    StateKindType,           # Enum: NORMAL, FINAL, HISTORY
)

# StateDef carries derived predicates:
state.is_leaf; state.is_composite; state.is_final; state.is_history; state.is_parallel

definition = StateMachineDefinition(settings=..., event_sources=[...], root_state=...)
json_str = definition.to_json(indent=2)
```

### Module: `smcraft.parser` (Spec 70)

```python
from smcraft.parser import StateMachineParser, EnrichedModel, ValidationError

parser = StateMachineParser()

model: EnrichedModel = parser.parse_file("input.smdf.json")   # auto-detects JSON/XML/FSM
definition = parser.parse_json(json_string)
definition = parser.parse_xml(xml_string)
model = parser.enrich(definition)

errors: list[ValidationError] = parser.validate(model)
for err in errors:
    print(f"[{err.rule_id}] {err.message} ({err.element})")
```

**EnrichedModel fields** — `definition`, `state_map` (name → state), `event_map` (id → event), `timer_map` (name → timer), `feeders_map` (feeder → events), `parent_map` (state → parent or None), `all_states` (tree order), `leaf_states`, `composite_states`.

**XML support:** parses the StateMachineDotNet-v1 namespace (`http://www.stateforge.com/StateMachineDotNet-v1`), namespaced and non-namespaced alike, including the legacy `.fsm` extension.

### Module: `smcraft.runtime` (Spec 71)

```python
from smcraft.runtime import (
    StateKind,          # LEAF=0, COMPOSITE=1, ROOT=2, FINAL=3, PARALLEL=4, HISTORY=5
    State, Context, ContextAsync, ContextBase, TransitionHelper,
    IObserver, ObserverNull, ObserverConsole, ObserverLogger,
)

state = State(name="Active", kind=StateKind.COMPOSITE, parent=root_state)
# Generated subclasses override on_entry(context) / on_exit(context).

ctx = Context(name="MyContext")
ctx.set_observer(ObserverConsole.instance())   # or ObserverLogger("mylogger")
ctx.register_end_handler(lambda c: print(f"{c.name} completed"))
ctx.enter_initial_state()                      # generated code overrides this

ctx.state_current   # active leaf state
ctx.state_previous  # last state before transition
ctx.state_history   # saved state for history support

ctx.start_timer("Timeout", 60000, lambda: ctx.on_timeout())
ctx.stop_timer("Timeout"); ctx.stop_all_timers()

data = ctx.serialize()   # {"state": "Active_WaitingSignal", "history": "..."}
ctx.deserialize(data)    # restores state_current via set_state()

# Async: events are queued and processed on a background thread.
actx = ContextAsync(name="AsyncContext", max_events=1024)
actx.schedule_event(handler_fn, *args)
```

**TransitionHelper** — the three-step move generated code performs:
```python
lca = TransitionHelper.find_common_ancestor(state_a, state_b)

# 1. Exit chain: walk from the current state up to the LCA, calling on_exit
TransitionHelper.process_transition_begin(context, state_prev, state_next, "EventName")
# 2. Set the new current state (generated code does this)
context.state_current = state_next
# 3. Entry chain: walk from the LCA down to the target, calling on_entry
TransitionHelper.process_transition_end(context, state_prev, state_next)
# Calls context._on_end() automatically when state_next is FINAL
```

**IObserver protocol** — `on_entry(context_name, state_name)`, `on_exit(…)`,
`on_transition_begin(context_name, state_prev, state_next, transition_name)`,
`on_transition_end(…)`, `on_timer_start(context_name, timer_name, duration)`,
`on_timer_stop(context_name, timer_name)`.

### Module: `smcraft.codegen` (Spec 72)

```python
from smcraft.codegen import PythonCodeGenerator, generate_python

# High-level:
code = generate_python("input.smdf.json", "output/machine_fsm.py")

# Low-level:
parser = StateMachineParser()
model = parser.parse_file("input.smdf.json")
code = PythonCodeGenerator(model).generate()
```

Generated structure:
1. `{Name}StateEnum(IntEnum)` — state enumeration
2. `State{Name}(State)` — base state class with virtual `on_{event}()` methods
3. `State{LeafName}(State{Name})` — one class per leaf state
4. `{Name}Context(Context)` — context class with state fields, object refs, `enter_initial_state()`, `set_state()`, `on_{event}()`
5. `{Feeder}` — feeder class with typed event methods

Naming: PascalCase → snake_case for Python identifiers (`OrderCreated` → `on_order_created`). Type mapping: string→str, int→int, float→float, bool→bool, object→Any.

### Module: `smcraft.cli` (Spec 72)

```bash
smcg <input-file> [--output|-o <dir>] [--language|-l python] [--name|-n <name>]
                  [--validate-only] [--verbose|-v]

smcg examples/bdbo_strategy.smdf.json -o output/ -v
smcg examples/fdb_breakout_strategy.smdf.json --validate-only
smcg input.smdf.json -l python -n MyMachine -o generated/
```

Output: `{output_dir}/{snake_case_name}_fsm.py`

## 4. TypeScript Engine Deep Dive (`@miadi/stateloom-engine` 0.4.3, npm)

### Installation
```bash
npm install @miadi/stateloom-engine
# or from source:
cd ts && npm install && npm run build
```

### Subpath Exports
```typescript
import { ... } from "smcraft";           // Barrel: all exports
import { ... } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/runtime";   // Runtime only
import { ... } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/machine";   // SMDF interpreter
import { ... } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/parser";    // Parser only
import { ... } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/codegen";   // Code generator only
```

### Model Types (`@miadi/stateloom-engine/model.ts`)
The §2 schema, as interfaces:
```typescript
interface StateMachineDefinition { settings: SettingsModel; events: EventSourceDef[]; state: StateDef }
interface SettingsModel { namespace: string; name?: string; asynchronous: boolean;
                          objects?: ObjectRef[]; context?: ContextConfig; using?: string[] }
interface StateDef { name: string; kind?: "normal" | "final" | "history"; description?: string;
                     onEntry?: { actions: ActionDef[] }; onExit?: { actions: ActionDef[] };
                     transitions?: TransitionDef[]; states?: StateDef[]; parallel?: ParallelDef }
interface TransitionDef { event: string; nextState?: string; condition?: string;
                          description?: string; actions?: ActionDef[] }
interface ActionDef { code?: string; timerStart?: { timer: string; duration: string }; timerStop?: string }
interface EventDef { id: string; name?: string; description?: string; parameters?: ParameterDef[] }
```

### Parser (`@miadi/stateloom-engine/parser`)
```typescript
import { parseJson, parseFile, enrich, validate, type EnrichedModel, type ValidationError } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/parser";

const definition = parseJson(jsonString);
const model: EnrichedModel = enrich(definition);
const errors: ValidationError[] = validate(model);

model.stateMap        // Map<string, StateDef>
model.eventMap        // Map<string, EventDef>
model.timerMap        // Map<string, TimerDef>
model.feedersMap      // Map<string, EventDef[]>
model.parentMap       // Map<string, string | null>
model.allStates       // StateDef[]
model.leafStates      // StateDef[]
model.compositeStates // StateDef[]
```

### Runtime (`@miadi/stateloom-engine/runtime`)
```typescript
import {
  State, StateKind, Context, ContextAsync, ContextBase,
  TransitionHelper, ObserverNull, ObserverConsole,
  type IObserver, type EndHandler
} from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/runtime";

// StateKind: LEAF, COMPOSITE, ROOT, FINAL, PARALLEL, HISTORY

const ctx = new Context("MyContext");
ctx.setObserver(ObserverConsole.instance());
ctx.registerEndHandler((c) => console.log(`${c.name} completed`));

// Same LCA algorithm as Python:
TransitionHelper.processTransitionBegin(context, statePrev, stateNext, "EventName");
TransitionHelper.processTransitionEnd(context, statePrev, stateNext);

// ContextAsync processes via queueMicrotask:
const asyncCtx = new ContextAsync("AsyncCtx", 1024);
asyncCtx.scheduleEvent(handler, ...args);

ctx.startTimer("Timeout", 60000, () => ctx.onTimeout());
ctx.stopTimer("Timeout");
ctx.stopAllTimers();

const data = ctx.serialize();
ctx.deserialize(data);
```

### Interpreter — `Machine` (`@miadi/stateloom-engine/machine`)

`Machine` drives a definition directly. No code generation, no build step — the drive-path contract external tools reach for when they hold an SMDF and want it to run.

```typescript
import { Machine, MachineDefinitionError } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/machine";

const machine = new Machine(definition, {
  name: "OrderFlow",
  observer: ObserverConsole.instance(),
  context: { canRetry: true },   // guard lookup table
  // guard: (condition, payload, context) => boolean
  // validate: true (default)
});

machine.state;                    // current leaf state name
machine.done;                     // true once a final state is reached
machine.visited;                  // leaf state names in visit order
machine.warnings;                 // non-fatal ValidationError[]
machine.availableEvents();        // event ids the current state can handle
machine.can("go");                // would send() be handled?
const r = machine.send("go", { orderId: "x" });
// r: { handled, changed, from, to, event, error? }
machine.setState("Active");       // restore a persisted position
machine.stop();                   // clear timers
```

Semantics, locked by `ts/src/tests/machine.test.ts`:

- Construction enters the initial state — first-child descent from root, skipping history pseudo-states.
- `send()` resolves the event from the current leaf upward through its ancestors; the **deepest** state declaring a matching transition wins.
- A transition without `nextState` is internal: `handled: true`, `changed: false`.
- A transition targeting the current state also resolves as internal — no exit / re-entry.
- A transition targeting a composite state descends to that composite's initial leaf.
- Guarded transitions are skipped unless the guard passes. The default guard is a truthy lookup of the condition string in `options.context`, and fails closed when no context is given.
- Reaching a `kind: "final"` state ends the machine; later sends return `handled: false`.
- `code` actions are NOT executed — they are strings meant for generated code. `timerStart` / `timerStop` run when the duration is numeric, and a fired timer sends its timer event id.

Validation on construction: V001 (no root), V002 (duplicate state) and V006 (unknown `nextState`) throw `MachineDefinitionError`, because a definition carrying any of them cannot be interpreted at all. Every other finding lands in `machine.warnings`.

### Code Generator (`@miadi/stateloom-engine/codegen`)
```typescript
import { TypeScriptCodeGenerator } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/codegen";
import { parseJson, enrich } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/parser";

const model = enrich(parseJson(jsonString));
const code: string = new TypeScriptCodeGenerator(model).generate();
```

Generates the TypeScript equivalent of the Python output: state enum, base state class, leaf state classes, context class, feeder classes.

---

## 5. The Real-Time Bridge

Spec 77 is the contract; this section is what shipped.

### 5.1 `@miadi/stateloom-protocol` 0.1.3

Zero runtime dependencies. Everything else in the loom depends on it, and it depends on nothing — which is why the same layout, the same edge routing and the same file names appear on every surface without any of them importing each other.

**PatchOp — the atomic vocabulary.** Op names mirror the MCP tools and the web store's granular actions. States are addressed by `name` (V002 makes that safe); events by `id`; parameters, transitions, actions and event sources positionally by index.

```typescript
type PatchOp =
  | { op: 'settings.update'; patch: Partial<SettingsModel> }
  | { op: 'state.add'; parent: string | null; state: StateDef; index?: number }
  | { op: 'state.update'; name: string; patch: Partial<Omit<StateDef, 'states' | 'transitions'>> }
  | { op: 'state.remove'; name: string }
  | { op: 'state.nest'; child: string; newParent: string }
  | { op: 'eventSource.add'; source: EventSourceDef; index?: number }
  | { op: 'eventSource.update'; index: number; patch: Partial<EventSourceDef> }
  | { op: 'eventSource.remove'; index: number }
  | { op: 'event.add'; sourceIndex: number; event: EventDef; index?: number }
  | { op: 'event.update'; id: string; patch: Partial<EventDef> }
  | { op: 'event.remove'; id: string }
  | { op: 'parameter.add'; eventId: string; parameter: ParameterDef; index?: number }
  | { op: 'parameter.update'; eventId: string; index: number; patch: Partial<ParameterDef> }
  | { op: 'parameter.remove'; eventId: string; index: number }
  | { op: 'transition.add'; state: string; transition: TransitionDef; index?: number }
  | { op: 'transition.update'; state: string; index: number; patch: Partial<TransitionDef> }
  | { op: 'transition.remove'; state: string; index: number }
  | { op: 'action.add'; state: string; hook: 'onEntry' | 'onExit'; action: ActionDef; index?: number }
  | { op: 'action.update'; state: string; hook: 'onEntry' | 'onExit'; index: number; action: ActionDef }
  | { op: 'action.remove'; state: string; hook: 'onEntry' | 'onExit'; index: number }
  | { op: 'runtime.enter'; state: string; from?: string; eventId?: string }
  | { op: 'runtime.exit'; state: string };
```

The two `runtime.*` ops are presentational — which state is lit up right now. `applyPatchOps` ignores them; they never mutate the definition.

**Wire names (`EV`)** — one source of truth shared by hub, CLI, web and agent clients. Inbound and outbound names deliberately overlap on the def channel so a peer can relay without renaming:

```typescript
export const EV = {
  // client → hub
  JOIN: 'bridge:join',        LEAVE: 'bridge:leave',
  PATCH_IN: 'def:patch',      FULL_IN: 'def:full',
  REQUEST: 'def:request',     PRESENCE_IN: 'presence:update',
  // hub → client
  WELCOME: 'bridge:welcome',  PATCH_OUT: 'def:patch',  FULL_OUT: 'def:full',
  ACK: 'def:ack',
  PRESENCE_JOIN: 'presence:join',   PRESENCE_LEAVE: 'presence:leave',
  PRESENCE_LIST: 'presence:list',   PRESENCE_UPDATE: 'presence:update',
  ERROR: 'bridge:error',
} as const;
```

**Envelopes:** `PatchEnvelope { docId, seq, baseSeq?, ops, origin, mtime? }`, `FullEnvelope { docId, seq, def, origin, mtime? }`, `DocSnapshot { docId, def, seq, mtime }`, `Presence { clientId, role, name?, color?, joinedAt }` with `role: 'agent' | 'cli' | 'web' | 'runtime'`. `colorFor(clientId)` derives a stable badge color from the id, so the same peer is the same color on every surface.

**Pure pairs:** `diffDefinitions(a, b) → PatchOp[]` and `applyPatchOps(def, ops) → def`. Both are pure, which is what lets the hub compute a patch for an edit that happened in an editor it never saw.

**Geometry:** `autoLayout` (deterministic box placement, `AUTO_LAYOUT_DEFAULTS`), `routeEdges` / `edgeCurve` / `selfLoopCurve` / `facingSides` / `portAt` / `bezier` (port assignment so two edges between the same pair get their own doors), `placeLabels` / `chipSize` / `glyphAt` / `guardText` (label chips settled so none prints through another), `eventGlyph` / `ALL_GLYPHS`.

**Render:** `renderMermaid(def)` and `renderAscii(def)` — text pictures with no dependency on a browser or a rasterizer.

**Naming:** `diagramFileName({ doc, machine, format, at })`, `timeStamp(at)`, `episodeOf(doc)`. See §8.

**Environment:** `envAlias(suffix, env?)` reads `STATELOOM_${suffix}` first, falls back to `SMCRAFT_${suffix}`. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` client reads cannot use it — Next.js inlines only literal accesses — so those keep an explicit `??` chain.

### 5.2 `@miadi/stateloom-client` 0.1.1

```typescript
import { createBridgeClient, type BridgeClient, type BridgeStatus } from "@miadi/stateloom-client";
```

A framework-agnostic socket.io-client wrapper: join a room, send patches, send a full definition, receive both, track presence, and auto-resync when a sequence gap says this client missed something. No React, no DOM.

### 5.3 `@miadi/stateloom` 0.1.1 — the hub

```bash
npx -y @miadi/stateloom            # bin: smcraft-bridge
smcraft-bridge --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4599
```

```typescript
import { startBridge, normalizeDocId, watchRoom, DEDUP_RING_SIZE } from "@miadi/stateloom";
const handle = await startBridge({ host, port, file });
```

What it holds:

- **One in-memory doc + seq per room.** Rooms are keyed by the **absolute project-file path**. This is why `set_project_file` moves the disk target and the bridge room together — they are the same identity.
- **Presence** — who is in the room, with role and color.
- **An external-edit differ.** chokidar watches the file; when someone edits the `.smdf.json` in a text editor, the hub diffs old against new and broadcasts the resulting `PatchOp[]`, so a hand edit arrives on the canvas as an ordinary patch.
- **mtime/hash dedup** over a ring of recent writes, so the hub does not echo back a change it just caused.

**The hub never writes disk.** Durability belongs to whoever made the edit. This keeps a crashed hub from being able to corrupt a document.

### 5.4 `@miadi/stateloom-react` 0.1.4

Peer dependency: `react ^19`.

```typescript
import {
  createBridgeSession, useSmcraftBridge,
  autoLayout, AUTO_LAYOUT_DEFAULTS,
  routeEdges, edgeCurve, selfLoopCurve, placeLabels, chipSize, eventGlyph,
  IDENTITY_VIEWPORT, VIEWPORT_LIMITS, fitToBoxes, panBy, zoomAt, zoomTo,
  screenToWorld, worldToScreen, viewportTransform, clampScale, normalizeViewport,
} from "@miadi/stateloom-react";
```

Two layers on purpose. `createBridgeSession` is the whole session with no React in it — unit-testable, no renderer. `useSmcraftBridge` wraps that core through `useSyncExternalStore`, which is what makes a live document a legitimate external store rather than a `useEffect` racing itself.

The drawing helpers are re-exported here rather than re-implemented: the designer canvas reaches for a curve or a label position at this address and should not have to know which package underneath the geometry lives in.

`viewport.ts` carries the pan/zoom math — `Viewport`, `Box`, `Point`, `ScaleLimits`, and the transforms between screen and world space.

### 5.5 `@miadi/stateloom-cli` 0.1.2 — `smcx`

```bash
npm i -g @miadi/stateloom-cli
```

Global options: `--bridge <url>` (default `envAlias("BRIDGE_URL")`), `--doc <path>` (default `envAlias("PROJECT_FILE")`), `--name <label>` (presence label).

```
smcx serve [--port n] [--host host] [--file path]
smcx add-state <name> [--parent name] [--kind normal|final|history] [--desc text]
smcx add-event <id> [--source index] [--desc text]
smcx add-transition <state> <event> [--to state] [--when cond]
smcx remove-state <name>
smcx load <file>
smcx watch [--as ascii|mermaid]
smcx render [--as svg|png|mermaid|ascii] [--out path|-] [--scale n]
            [--theme dark|light] [--title text] [--stamp] [--open]
smcx open [--web url]
smcx presence
```

Every mutation is **durable-first**: persist to disk, then emit to the hub. The order matters — it means a mutation issued while the hub is down is still a real edit, and the hub's own file watcher will pick it up when it returns.

`render` reads the durable `.smdf.json` straight off disk: no hub, no browser, no agent needed. It prints the absolute path it wrote.

### 5.6 `@miadi/stateloom-mcp` 0.1.3 — see §6

The MCP server is a bridge client like any other. It depends on `stateloom-cli` (for the render path), `stateloom-client` and `stateloom-protocol`.

---

## 6. MCP Server Deep Dive

### Installation & Setup

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "stateloom": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@miadi/stateloom-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "STATELOOM_PROJECT_FILE": "/absolute/path/to/machine.smdf.json",
        "STATELOOM_BRIDGE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:4599"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`scripts/live-loop.sh mcp-line` prints the equivalent `claude mcp add` invocation with the absolute paths already resolved.

The package ships two bins: `stateloom-mcp` and `smcraft-mcp`. The second is the pre-rename name, kept so an existing registration does not break.

### The 15 tools

**Build**

| Tool | Parameters | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `create_state_machine` | `namespace` ✓, `name` ✓, `asynchronous?` | Writes the definition with a Root state and an empty `Internal` event source. |
| `add_state` | `name` ✓, `parent?` (default `Root`), `kind?` (`normal`\|`final`\|`history`), `description?` | Errors when no definition exists yet, or the parent is not found. |
| `add_event` | `id` ✓, `description?` | Added to the first event source (`Internal`). |
| `add_transition` | `state` ✓, `event` ✓, `nextState?`, `condition?`, `description?` | Omit `nextState` for an internal transition. Returns `Idle --[Start]--> Active`. Errors when the state is not found. |
| `remove_state` | `name` ✓ | Removes the state and its children. Cannot remove `Root`. |

**Read**

| Tool | Parameters | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `get_definition` | — | JSON string with the full definition under `stateMachine`. |
| `load_definition` | `json` ✓ | Accepts `{ "stateMachine": … }`, `{ "StateMachine": … }` or a raw definition. Confirms name, state count, event count. |
| `list_states` | — | Indented tree: state name, kind, transition count, each transition as → [event] → target. |
| `list_events` | — | Flat list of event ids with descriptions. |

**Act**

#### `validate_definition()`
Returns `✓ Definition is valid`, or a list of `[V00x]` messages.

#### `generate_code(language: "python" | "typescript")`
Returns the generated source as text. Validation errors must be resolved first. Tries the `smcg` CLI, then falls back to a lightweight inline generator.

#### `generate_rispec(intent?: string)`
Returns a RISE rispec in markdown; `intent` overrides the desired outcome. When the SMDF carries `settings._source.pdeId` / `pdeFolder`, the originating PDE's intent, directions and ambiguities are folded into the spec. This is the Exportation terminus of Spec 76: a machine designed from a decomposed prompt can write back the specification that prompt was reaching for.

#### `render_diagram(format?, path?, scale?, theme?, stamp?, open?)`
```
format: "png" | "svg" | "mermaid" | "ascii"   (default png)
path:   override the output location          scale: pixel multiplier for png
theme:  "dark" | "light"                      stamp: name each render, don't overwrite
open:   hand the file to the platform viewer
```
Writes next to the project document (or at `path`) and returns the absolute path, byte count, pixel dimensions and which backend drew it. For `png` under 1,500,000 bytes the image itself rides back inside the tool result — an agent can look at what it just designed without leaving the conversation. Past that limit it gets the path alone, because a multi-megabyte base64 blob would crowd out the conversation it was meant to illustrate.

**Document**

#### `set_project_file(path: string)`
`path` must end in `.json`; the convention is `*.smdf.json`. Chooses which document the loom weaves — disk persistence **and** the live bridge room both re-point, because the hub keys rooms by this path. A missing file is legitimate: `create_state_machine` or `load_definition` writes it next. Reports the new path, the previous one, a summary of what is there, and the bridge's state.

#### `get_project_file()`
Reports the active document path, whether it exists on disk, and live-bridge status.

### Resource
`smcraft://definition` (`application/json`) — the current definition as JSON, or an error when none is loaded.

### Prompt
`design-state-machine(domain?, name?)` — a guided conversation: create → identify states → define events → wire transitions → validate → generate. `domain` is context such as "trading" or "order processing".

### Design session protocol
1. **Point** — `set_project_file` (or let `STATELOOM_PROJECT_FILE` do it)
2. **Initialize** — `create_state_machine` or `load_definition`
3. **Build** — iterate `add_state` → `add_event` → `add_transition`
4. **Look** — `render_diagram` and read the picture back
5. **Validate** — `validate_definition` → resolve errors → re-validate
6. **Export** — `generate_code` for runnable output, `generate_rispec` for the specification

---

```bash
npx -y @miadi/stateloom-skills skills list
npx -y @miadi/stateloom-skills skills install stateloom-design
npx -y @miadi/stateloom-skills skills install --all
```

`install` copies a ready-to-use `SKILL.md` into `.claude/skills/`, so an agent that has never seen this system arrives already knowing how to drive it. The sources live in `./skills/` in this repository and are synced into the package at build/pack time.

Six skills, one per surface of the system:

- `stateloom-setup`
- `stateloom-design`
- `stateloom-live-loop`
- `stateloom-render`
- `stateloom-codegen`
- `stateloom-rispec`

The package also exports `@miadi/stateloom-skills/catalog` for programmatic access to the skill list.

## 8. Rendering and Export Naming

### Three surfaces, one board

- **CLI** — `smcx render` reads the durable `.smdf.json` off disk and prints the absolute path it wrote. No hub, no browser, no agent.
- **MCP** — `render_diagram` writes the same file and hands the picture back inside the tool result.
- **Web designer** — the format picker beside 📥 exports PNG, JPEG, SVG, Mermaid (`.mmd`) or Markdown (`.md`, the same graph inside a ```` ```mermaid ```` fence).

The picture formats from the canvas take the board as it stands, hand-dragged boxes included. The two text formats come from the definition, since Mermaid describes a graph and carries no placement. CLI and MCP derive their layout with the same `autoLayout` that sits behind ⤢ Arrange, so all three agree on where the boxes are.

```bash
smcx render --as png --scale 2 --open   # → /path/to/statemachine.png
smcx render --as svg                    # needs no rasterizer at all
smcx render --as mermaid --out -        # to stdout, for a README
smcx render --as png --stamp            # → ep252--Film--260730175243.png
```

### The PNG rasterizer chain

`svg`, `mermaid` and `ascii` need nothing installed. `png` goes through whichever backend the host actually has, tried in this order, and the result reports which one drew it:

1. **sharp** — used when the optional module is importable. It is never a static import: nothing declares it, so the type-checker and bundlers must not chase it.
2. **rsvg-convert** (librsvg)
3. **inkscape**
4. **magick** (ImageMagick 7)
5. **convert** (ImageMagick 6)
6. **google-chrome** / **chromium** / **chromium-browser**, headless

### Export names

A browser download always, and `--stamp` / `stamp: true` on demand, produce:

```
[ep252--]<Machine>--<yyMMddHHmmss>.<ext>

ep252--InteractiveProduction--260730175243.svg
└ episode  └ machine            └ yyMMddHHmmss
```

Three questions answered at a glance: where the work belongs, what it draws, and when it was drawn. `statemachine.png`, rewritten every time, is a file you lose.

- The episode prefix appears only when the document lives under one — `<episode>/diagrams/<name>.smdf.json`, the miadi-chronicle convention. A machine outside the chronicle has no prefix to carry.
- Seconds are in the stamp because a designer exporting a PNG and then an SVG of the same board does it inside one minute, and two names differing only by extension read as one name.
- The name falls back machine name → document name → `statemachine`.
- `diagramFileName` is pure — the clock is an argument, never a call. Same inputs, same name.

Built once in `bridge-protocol/src/exportName.ts`, so every surface names files alike.

---

## 9. Environment Contract

`bridge-protocol/src/env.ts` and `scripts/live-loop.sh` are the two halves. `STATELOOM_*` is read first; the legacy `SMCRAFT_*` twin is honored as a fallback, and the launcher exports **both** twins from one resolved value, so a process of either generation reads the same thing.

| Variable | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `STATELOOM_PROJECT_FILE` | `$REPO/statemachine.smdf.json` | **Must be absolute.** |
| `STATELOOM_BRIDGE_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | |
| `STATELOOM_BRIDGE_PORT` | `4599` | The hub. |
| `STATELOOM_BRIDGE_URL` | `http://$HOST:$PORT` | |
| `STATELOOM_WEB_PORT` | `4598` | The canvas. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_STATELOOM_BRIDGE_URL` | mirrors `BRIDGE_URL` | Inlined at web **build** time — a running server cannot flip it. |

**Why absolute.** `mcp/src/server.ts` and `web/src/lib/projectFile.ts` each resolve the project file against their own cwd. Two processes, two cwds, one relative path, and the divergence is silent — it presents as "○ no disk" on the canvas while the agent is happily writing somewhere else. `scripts/live-loop.sh` computes absolute paths once and hands the same values to every process, writing them to `.env.smcraft-live` where they can be read back.

```bash
scripts/live-loop.sh env         # print resolved exports (eval-able)
scripts/live-loop.sh hub         # start the socket hub (foreground)
scripts/live-loop.sh web-build   # build web with the bridge URL inlined
scripts/live-loop.sh web         # start the built web app (foreground)
scripts/live-loop.sh mcp-line    # print the MCP registration line
```

4598 (web canvas) and 4599 (hub) sit together as the loom's pair of ports.

---

## 10. Runtime Engine Details

### LCA-based transitions
Every transition computes the Lowest Common Ancestor of source and target, then:

1. **Exit chain** — walk from the source state UP to the LCA (exclusive), calling `on_exit()` at each level
2. **Notify** — observer receives `on_transition_begin`
3. **Set current state** to the target
4. **Entry chain** — walk from the LCA DOWN to the target, calling `on_entry()` at each level
5. **Notify** — observer receives `on_transition_end`
6. **Check final** — if the target is FINAL, `_on_end()` fires every registered end handler

Example, `Active_WaitingSignal → Completed`:
```
Exit:  Active_WaitingSignal.on_exit()
Exit:  Active.on_exit()               (parent — up to LCA = Root)
Observer: transition_begin
Entry: Completed.on_entry()           (from LCA = Root down)
Observer: transition_end
→ Completed is FINAL → fire end handlers
```

### Hierarchical entry chain
`enter_initial_state()` walks from Root down to the deepest initial child — first child of first child of first child — calling `on_entry()` at each level.

### Event dispatch
Generated contexts expose `on_{event}()` which delegates to `self.state_current.on_{event}()`. The leaf state class holds the transition logic, guard conditions included.

### Timers
`threading.Timer` with daemon threads (Python), `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` (TypeScript). Timer events are synthetic events that call the corresponding `on_{timer_event}()` handler; `stop_all_timers()` cleans up on teardown.

### Observer hook points
State lifecycle `on_entry` / `on_exit`, transition lifecycle `on_transition_begin` / `on_transition_end`, timer lifecycle `on_timer_start` / `on_timer_stop`. ObserverConsole format: `ContextName: enter StateName`, `ContextName: transition begin StateA -> StateB [EventName]`.

### Async context behavior
- Events are enqueued as `(handler, args)` tuples
- Processed sequentially on a background thread (Python) or via `queueMicrotask` (TypeScript)
- Maximum 1024 events per processing cycle, configurable
- Errors are logged but do not stop event processing
- Thread-safe via `threading.Lock` (Python)

---

## 11. Code Generator Pipeline

```
Input File (.smdf.json / .smdf.xml / .fsm)
    ↓
StateMachineParser.parse_file(path)
    ↓  auto-detects format; derives name from filename when absent
EnrichedModel
    ↓  state_map, event_map, timer_map, feeders_map, parent_map
StateMachineParser.validate(model)
    ↓  V001–V014 → list[ValidationError]
PythonCodeGenerator(model).generate()  |  TypeScriptCodeGenerator(model).generate()
    ↓
Source Code (string)
    ↓
Output File ({snake_case_name}_fsm.py or .ts)
```

### Generated file structure (Python target)
```python
"""
Generated State Machine: OrderWorkflow
Namespace: MyApp

Generated by SMCG. Do not edit manually.
"""

from enum import IntEnum
from smcraft.runtime import Context, ObserverNull, State, StateKind, TransitionHelper

class OrderWorkflowStateEnum(IntEnum):
    ROOT = 0; PENDING = 1; ACTIVE = 2; COMPLETED = 3

class StateOrderWorkflow(State):
    """Base state with virtual event handlers."""
    def on_order_created(self, context, order_id: str) -> None: pass
    def on_order_approved(self, context) -> None: pass

class StatePending(StateOrderWorkflow):
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__(name="Pending", kind=StateKind.LEAF, parent=parent)

    def on_order_created(self, context, order_id: str) -> None:
        TransitionHelper.process_transition_begin(context, self, context.state_active, "OrderCreated")
        context.state_current = context.state_active
        TransitionHelper.process_transition_end(context, self, context.state_active)

class OrderWorkflowContext(Context):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(name="OrderWorkflowContext")
        self.state_root = State(name="Root", kind=StateKind.ROOT, parent=None)
        self.state_pending = StatePending(parent=self.state_root)
        self.state_active = StateActive(parent=self.state_root)

    def enter_initial_state(self) -> None:
        self.state_current = self.state_pending
        self.observer.on_entry(self.name, "Root");    self.state_root.on_entry(self)
        self.observer.on_entry(self.name, "Pending"); self.state_pending.on_entry(self)

    def on_order_created(self, order_id: str) -> None:
        if self.state_current:
            self.state_current.on_order_created(self, order_id)

class OrderFeeder:
    """Event feeder. Provides typed event methods."""
    def __init__(self, context: OrderWorkflowContext): self.context = context
    def order_created(self, order_id: str) -> None: self.context.on_order_created(order_id)
```

### Multi-transition guard logic
When a state carries several transitions for one event with conditions:
```python
def on_strategy_failed(self, context, error: str) -> None:
    if strategy.can_retry():
        TransitionHelper.process_transition_begin(context, self, context.state_active_waiting_signal, "StrategyFailed[strategy.can_retry()]")
        context.state_current = context.state_active_waiting_signal
        TransitionHelper.process_transition_end(context, self, context.state_active_waiting_signal)
    else:
        TransitionHelper.process_transition_begin(context, self, context.state_failed, "StrategyFailed")
        context.state_current = context.state_failed
        TransitionHelper.process_transition_end(context, self, context.state_failed)
```

### Generation vs. interpretation
Two ways to run a definition, and they are not competitors:

- **Generate** (`smcg`, `generate_code`) — standalone source that imports only the runtime library. Ship it, read it, step through it in a debugger, edit the actions by hand.
- **Interpret** (`@miadi/stateloom-engine/machine`) — hold the definition in memory and `send()` events at it. No build step, so a machine edited on the canvas a second ago is the machine you are driving now. `code` actions are inert here; they are strings for the generated path.

---

## 12. Web Designer (`web/`, private)

`"private": true` — it is not published. Run it from the repo.

```bash
cd web && npm install && npm run dev
# http://localhost:4598  (4598 canvas / 4599 hub are the loom's pair)
```

### Stack
Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19 with the React Compiler, Zustand 5, SVG canvas, Tailwind CSS 4, and `@miadi/stateloom-react` for the live document.

### Components

**`Canvas.tsx`** — the SVG rendering surface. Flattens the hierarchy with `collectAllStates(definition.state)`. States are rounded rectangles with kind indicators (dashed for final, badges for entry/exit actions); transitions are Bézier curves routed through assigned ports so two edges between the same pair each get their own door. Draw mode: click source → click target → event picker. Drag-to-move with position persistence. Right-click context menu. Validation errors as red borders and a ⚠ icon. Keyboard: Delete, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, Escape.

**`Toolbar.tsx`** — Open / Save / Export with a format picker, Select ↔ Draw mode toggle, +State, Delete, Validate, Generate, Undo, Redo, ⤢ Arrange (`autoLayout`).

**`PropertiesPanel.tsx`** — the selected state or transition: name, kind, description, entry/exit action list, and for transitions the event, target, condition and description. **`EventsPanel.tsx`** — events with their parameters. **`SettingsPanel.tsx`** — namespace, name, asynchronous toggle, object references. **`ValidationPanel.tsx`** — rule ids and messages, click-to-select the errored state. **`CodePreview.tsx`** — generated code with a Python/TypeScript selector and copy-to-clipboard.

### Store
A Zustand store holds the definition, state positions, selection, undo/redo history, validation errors, canvas mode and the generated-code cache. Granular actions map one-to-one onto the PatchOp vocabulary, which is what lets a local edit and a remote patch take the same path into the document.

---

## 13. RISE Specifications

**[70 — SMDF Format](./rispecs/70-smdf-format.spec.md)** — schema, state types (leaf, composite, final, history, parallel, root), validation V001–V014, JSON primary with XML legacy. The canonical representation every package consumes.

**[71 — Runtime Engine](./rispecs/71-runtime-engine.spec.md)** — State with StateKind, Context, ContextAsync, TransitionHelper (LCA algorithm, entry/exit chains), the IObserver protocol. Timers via `threading.Timer` / `setTimeout`. State serialization. The `Machine` interpreter extends this spec.

**[72 — Code Generator (SMCG)](./rispecs/72-code-generator.spec.md)** — SMDF → Parser → EnrichedModel → Validator → CodeGenerator → output. Python and TypeScript targets. CLI `smcg`.

**[73 — MCP Server](./rispecs/73-mcp-server.spec.md)** — the tool surface, the design session protocol, and "Path Power": the `set_project_file` / `get_project_file` contract by which an agent chooses the active document mid-session and the bridge room follows it.

**[74 — Web Designer](./rispecs/74-web-designer.spec.md)** — canvas, store, components, position tracking, undo/redo, composite drill-down.

**[75 — Agent-Designer Bridge](./rispecs/75-agent-designer-bridge.spec.md)** — the first bridge design: live sync over Socket.IO with the MCP server as single source of truth, plus a file-I/O scaffold pipeline. Spec 77 supersedes its sync model with granular patches and a hub that owns no truth.

**[76 — RISE Rispec Generator](./rispecs/76-rise-rispec-generator.spec.md)** — SMDF as the exportation terminus of RISE. `generate_rispec` turns a designed machine back into a specification, folding in the originating PDE's intent when the definition carries `settings._source`.

**[77 — Real-Time Design Bridge](./rispecs/77-realtime-design-bridge.spec.md)** — granular bidirectional sync: the PatchOp vocabulary, the pure diff/apply pair, sequence numbers and resync, presence, the external-edit differ, durable-first ordering.

**[78 — Forgewright Episode Rendering](./rispecs/78-forgewright-episode-rendering.plan.md)** (plan) — rendering episode state machines for the chronicle: where diagrams live, how they are named, which surface draws them.

**[79 — Layout Persistence](./rispecs/79-layout-persistence.plan.md)** (plan) — carrying hand-placed box positions in the document, so a board arranged by a person survives a reload and reaches the other surfaces.

---

## 14. KINSHIP Relationships

### Identity
SMCraft is the **Architect's Toolkit** — it does not trade, analyze or decide. It provides the structural framework other systems use to organize their state transitions with correctness guarantees.

### Upstream (Feeds From)
- **caishen** — the original C# StateForge runtime patterns and SMCG code generation. RISE Specs 60-63 define the contracts SMCraft reimplements.

### Downstream (Feeds Into)
- **jgt-strategy-api** — the 13-state FDB Breakout Strategy FSM (CREATED → WAITING_BREAKOUT → … → COMPLETED) designed using smcraft patterns; `src/fsm.py` follows the hierarchical architecture.
- **jgt-code** — terminal trading agent, imports `smcraft` for the TypeScript runtime.
- **mia-code-server** — creative process stages (Germination → Assimilation → Completion) as hierarchical state machines.
- **jgtutils** — previously hosted the Python state machine code; now imports `smcraft` as a dependency.
- **Any application** — SMCraft is domain-agnostic.

### Siblings
**jgtml** (ML pipelines) and **jgtapy** (indicators) — sibling tooling and library packages.

### Conceptual Bridges

#### Structural Tension ↔ State Transitions
Structural Tension Charts are structurally isomorphic to state machines:

| STC Concept | State Machine Equivalent |
|-------------|--------------------------|
| Desired Outcome | Target/Final State |
| Current Reality | Initial State |
| Action Step Completion | Transition Event |
| Structural Tension | Disequilibrium energy driving state toward resolution |
| Resolution | Reaching the final state |

#### Creative Process ↔ Composite State Machine
mia-code-server's creative process maps to a composite state machine where each phase (Germination, Assimilation, Completion) is a composite state containing sub-states — Germination holding TaskDefinition, SpecGeneration, PDEDecomposition.

### Medicine Wheel Alignment
- **EAST**: designer detects workflow patterns (inquiry & vision)
- **SOUTH**: parser analyzes and validates definitions (planning & consent)
- **WEST**: code generator transforms to executable form (experience & action)
- **NORTH**: runtime executes the state machine (reflection & wisdom)

---

## 15. Example State Machines

### BDBO Strategy (`examples/bdbo_strategy.smdf.json`)
Trading strategy demonstrating a composite state (Active with three children), timer events, onEntry/onExit actions, guard conditions (`strategy.can_retry()`) and multiple transitions per event.

### FDB Breakout Strategy (`examples/fdb_breakout_strategy.smdf.json`)
A 13-state trading FSM with three object references (strategy, market, broker), 14 typed events, a timer (MaxPuiTimer), a deep composite hierarchy (Active with six children), six final states, guard conditions, and retry logic (Active_EntryOrderCanceled → Active_WaitingSignal under `cancel_count < max_cancel`).

### Chronicle machines
miadi-chronicle episodes host their machines at `<episode>/diagrams/<name>.smdf.json` — the convention `episodeOf()` reads to build the `ep252--` export prefix. First proven inhabitant: ep103's `film-preprod`. ep090 predates the convention with six machines under `state-machines/*.smcraft.json`; see `docs/reviews/` for the reconciliation recommendation. Handoff history is in `docs/handoffs/`.

---

## 16. Quick Starts

### Engine — Python
```bash
pip install smcraft
smcg examples/bdbo_strategy.smdf.json -o output/ -v

python -c "
from smcraft import StateMachineParser
from smcraft.codegen import PythonCodeGenerator
model = StateMachineParser().parse_file('examples/bdbo_strategy.smdf.json')
print(PythonCodeGenerator(model).generate()[:200])
"
```

### Engine — TypeScript
```typescript
import { parseJson, enrich, validate } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/parser";
import { TypeScriptCodeGenerator } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/codegen";
import { Machine } from "@miadi/stateloom-engine/machine";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

const definition = parseJson(readFileSync("examples/bdbo_strategy.smdf.json", "utf-8"));
const model = enrich(definition);
console.log(`${model.allStates.length} states, ${validate(model).length} errors`);

const code = new TypeScriptCodeGenerator(model).generate();   // generate it…

const machine = new Machine(definition, { context: { canRetry: true } });  // …or run it
machine.send("Activate");
console.log(machine.state, machine.done);
```

### MCP server
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "stateloom": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@miadi/stateloom-mcp"],
      "env": { "STATELOOM_PROJECT_FILE": "/abs/path/machine.smdf.json" }
    }
  }
}
```
Then, in conversation:
```
create_state_machine(namespace="MyApp", name="OrderFlow")
add_state(name="Pending")
add_state(name="Active")
add_state(name="Completed", kind="final")
add_event(id="Start")
add_transition(state="Pending", event="Start", nextState="Active")
validate_definition()
render_diagram(format="png")        # look at it
generate_code(language="python")
```

### The live loop
```bash
export STATELOOM_PROJECT_FILE=/abs/path/machine.smdf.json
scripts/live-loop.sh hub                                      # hub on 4599
scripts/live-loop.sh web-build && scripts/live-loop.sh web    # canvas on 4598
scripts/live-loop.sh mcp-line                                 # the agent registration line
smcx watch                                                    # the doc as ASCII, live
```
An agent's `add_state`, a `smcx add-transition` and a drag on the canvas all land in the same document, and each surface sees the others arrive.

### Agent skills
```bash
npx -y @miadi/stateloom-skills skills install --all
```

---

## 17. For LLMs

### When to use SMCraft
Designing a stateful workflow with hierarchical states, events and transitions; generating executable state machine code from a declarative definition; running a definition directly without a build step (`@miadi/stateloom-engine/machine`); validating structure before anything is generated; designing a machine collaboratively with a human who is watching a canvas.

### Key design decisions
1. **SMDF is the single source of truth** — every package parses the same format.
2. **Hierarchical, not flat** — composite states, parallel regions, history states.
3. **LCA-based transitions** — correct entry/exit chain semantics for nested states.
4. **Generation and interpretation both ship** — generate standalone code, or drive the definition in memory.
5. **Observer pattern for monitoring** — no modification to machine logic needed.
6. **The hub owns no truth** — it sequences and broadcasts; durability belongs to the editor that made the change.
7. **Rooms are keyed by absolute path** — document identity and room identity are the same thing.
8. **Domain-agnostic** — no trading or domain concepts in the framework itself.

### Common patterns
- **Guard conditions** — several transitions on one event with `condition` fields become if/elif/else chains in generated code, and ordered guard evaluation in the interpreter.
- **Timer events** — define the timer in the event source, use `timerStart` / `timerStop` in actions; the timer fires as an ordinary event.
- **Object references** — `settings.objects` entries are reachable as `context.{instance}.method()` inside action code.
- **Feeder classes** — the generated typed API for sending events into the machine.
- **Async mode** — `asynchronous: true` generates ContextAsync with an event queue.
- **PDE provenance** — carry `settings._source.pdeId` / `pdeFolder` and `generate_rispec` writes the specification with the originating intent folded in.

### File naming conventions
Definitions `{name}.smdf.json` · generated Python `{snake_case_name}_fsm.py` · generated TypeScript `{snake_case_name}_fsm.ts` · stamped exports `[ep252--]<Machine>--<yyMMddHHmmss>.<ext>` · chronicle machines `<episode>/diagrams/<name>.smdf.json`.

## Cross-Repository Links

- [Master LLM Index](https://llms.jgwill.com/llms-full.txt): Guidance portfolio — STC ↔ FSM equivalence documentation
- [RISE Framework](https://llms.jgwill.com/llms-rise-framework.txt): Specification methodology for rispecs 60-79
- [Structural Tension Charts](https://llms.jgwill.com/llms-structural-tension-charts.txt): STC methodology — conceptual isomorphism with FSM (desired outcome = target state)
- [Veritas](https://docs.veritas.jgwill.com/llms.txt): MMOT evaluation format — smcraft-evaluation.tandt.json is a Veritas Type 2 model for self-assessment
